parties.petitioner: I Pay Clearing Services Private Limited

summary: The appellant challenged the Bombay High Court's dismissal of its application under Section 34(4) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seeking remand to the arbitrator for additional reasons on the issue of illegal termination of contract. The award granted Rs.50 crores and 18% interest due to abrupt termination, but ICICI Bank contested on grounds of accord and satisfaction. The Supreme Court examined whether defective reasoning without a finding on a key issue constitutes a curable defect under Section 34(4). The dispute centered on adequacy of reasoning in arbitration awards and the scope of judicial intervention.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
Kinnari Mullick and Anr. v. Ghanshyam Das Damani
Dyna Technologies Pvt. Ltd. v. Crompt met Greaves Ltd.
Som Datt Builders Limited v. State of Kerala
Permasteelisa Pacific Holdings Ltd. v. Hyundai Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd.
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed to the extent of remitting the matter to the Arbitrator to record proper reasons on the issue of illegal and abrupt termination, under Section 34(4) of the Act, to cure the defect in the award, without disturbing the quantum of compensation.
